title: The agent loop
summary: An agent is a model calling tools in a loop until the goal is done or a limit is hit.

steps.label: goal
steps.title: You give a goal, not steps
steps.text: With a plain chatbot you drive. With an agent you state the outcome and the model works out the steps.
payload: "Summarise this week's open bugs into report.md"
A hard stop so a confused agent can't loop forever.

steps.label: turn 1
steps.title: Turn 1: think, then act
steps.text: The runtime sends the goal and the tool list. The model reasons about what it needs first.
payload: Small now; it grows every turn.

steps.label: tool_use
steps.title: The model picks a tool
steps.text: It chooses list_issues with a filter. The runtime runs it.

steps.label: list_issues
steps.title: Observe
steps.text: The result is appended to the conversation. This think → act → observe cycle is often called ReAct.
payload: 12 issues · #481 login timeout · #477 CSV export blank · …

steps.label: 12 issues
steps.title: The loop continues
steps.text: The model sees the list, decides it needs detail on the three highest-priority bugs, and requests read_issue three times. Several independent calls can run in parallel.
payload: Every result makes the next call bigger and pricier.

steps.label: write_file
steps.title: Produce the deliverable
steps.text: Once it has enough, the model asks to write the report. Writing is an action with side effects, so many runtimes ask for confirmation here.

steps.label: turn 6
steps.title: Check if done
steps.text: After the write succeeds the model reviews the goal and replies with text instead of a tool call. That's the signal to stop.
payload: Text with no tool call ends the loop.

steps.label: done
steps.title: Report ready
steps.text: Real agents add retries, timeouts, cost budgets and logging around this same simple loop.
